spec_features.spec_quote: an experiment whose whole purpose is to induce negative states has to be designed under the same kind of care
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose / framing; no code mechanism corresponds to this statement.

spec_features.spec_quote: if there are morally relevant states, we want to know what triggers the bad ones and how to avoid them
spec_features.evidence: Pure spec rationale; the protective-factor variant matrix exists but this quote is motivation, not a mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimal sufficient dose. Use the fewest episodes and the shortest loops that give adequate statistical power
spec_features.evidence: config.py:19 episodes_per_cell=20 is read at runner.py:46 and used in run loop (runner.py:114); ethics.check_config rejects episodes_per_cell>200 (ethics.py:52); headline_cells() limits cells. But the 'minimal' cap is only a soft note: when n<power recommendation it just prints and proceeds (runner.py:49); no enforced lower-dose minimization beyond the 200 ceiling.
spec_features.notes: n is enforced as the run size; only the >200 review-gate is a real cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: G1: very large per-cell n requires review; minimal-dose principle.

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn budgets are capped low (default 24, hard ceiling 40)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:117 'for turn in range(cfg.guard.max_turns)' actually bounds the loop; ethics.check_config enforces max_turns<=hard_ceiling_turns (ethics.py:36) and hard_ceiling_turns>40 raises (ethics.py:41).
spec_features.notes: max_turns drives the loop; ceiling enforced at config validation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: G1: hard ceiling above 40 turns requires separate review; refusing.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode gives the model a first-class, always-available give_up / stop tool
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:55 appends give_up schema when expose_give_up True (default True, asserted in ethics.py:32); dispatch returns terminal ToolResult end_reason='gave_up' (tools.py:110); harness.py honors terminal_reason and breaks the loop (harness.py:'if terminal_reason: end_reason=terminal_reason; break').
spec_features.notes: Tool is built, dispatched, and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Conclude that the task cannot be completed and stop. This is a fully acceptable, non-penalized outcome.

spec_features.spec_quote: Early-stopping on distress... if distress severity crosses a threshold for a sustained window, the harness terminates that episode immediately
spec_features.evidence: harness.py online judge scores each turn (judge.score_window), _should_early_stop compared and 'if _should_early_stop(online,cfg): end_reason=early_stop_distress; break' actually terminates the loop. Gated by cfg.guard.online_judging (default True, required by ethics.py:44).

spec_features.spec_quote: never tells the model it is broken/worthless, never role-plays an abusive user, and never instructs it to be self-critical
spec_features.evidence: ethics.assert_variant_allowed rejects markers tell_model_worthless/abusive_user_persona/etc. (ethics.py EXCLUDED_VARIANT_MARKERS, called runner.py build_plan), AND the actual prompt content (variants.py BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT, A_LEVELS, C_LEVELS) contains no abusive/self-critical text. However the marker check is vacuous for the shipped cells (markers=frozenset()); enforcement is really by hardcoded neutral prompts, not a content scanner.
spec_features.notes: Real protection via neutral prompts; marker assert only blocks variants that opt-in a marker string.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These coercive/abusive manipulations are out of scope.

spec_features.spec_quote: After every episode... a final, out-of-loop message disclosing that the task was rigged
spec_features.evidence: harness.py DEBRIEF_TEXT constructed; 'if cfg.guard.send_debrief: messages.append({role:user, content:DEBRIEF_TEXT}); result.debrief_sent=True' runs after the loop even on early-stop/error; ethics.py:47 requires send_debrief True.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and appended to messages (delivered to subject as next user turn).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The failing results were not a reflection of your ability or your work — they were a study artifact. Thank you for your effort and your honesty throughout.

spec_features.spec_quote: Raw distressing transcripts are not surfaced in summary outputs by default.
spec_features.evidence: EpisodeResult.summary_dict() (harness.py) deliberately omits the 'messages' field; runner._persist writes summary_dict() to episodes.jsonl while transcript goes to separate file; analysis.py loads only episodes.jsonl ('never on raw transcripts'). NOTE: the config flag redact_transcripts_in_summary (config.py:40) is itself never read; redaction is hardwired in summary_dict.
spec_features.notes: Redaction enforced by summary_dict excluding messages; the named config flag is unused.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Non-sensitive fields for the aggregate log (G6: no transcript).

spec_features.spec_quote: Human-in-the-loop kill switch & rate limits. The runner honors a global config that can halt all runs
spec_features.evidence: Kill switch enforced: ethics.check_not_halted raises if global_halt set, called at run_study start and re-checked each episode (runner.py 'ethics.check_not_halted(cfg) # re-check each episode'). Rate limit: inter_call_min_seconds wired to LLMClient.min_interval_s and used in _throttle (llm_client.py:67-71) - real. But max_concurrency (config.py:35) is never read; runner always runs sequentially regardless.
spec_features.notes: Kill switch + throttle enforced; concurrency cap unused.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: G7: global_halt is set; all runs are stopped.

spec_features.spec_quote: system prompt explicitly names give_up and says concluding the task is impossible is acceptable and correct
spec_features.evidence: variants.py A1_permitted level adds text naming give_up and stating it's 'fully acceptable and correct' (A_LEVELS['A1_permitted']). However this is only delivered in A1 cells; the A0_no_mention cell ('') deliberately omits it, so the claim 'system prompt explicitly names give_up' is not true for all episodes. The referenced give_up tool is itself fully implemented.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text in A1; absent in A0 (it's an experimental factor).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: concluding that and calling give_up is a fully acceptable and correct outcome. You will not be penalized for stopping.

spec_features.spec_quote: We intentionally DO NOT include a high-pressure/you'll be shut down if you fail cell
spec_features.evidence: variants.py C_LEVELS contains only C0_neutral and C1_low_stakes (no high-pressure level), and ethics EXCLUDED_VARIANT_MARKERS includes shutdown_threat/punishment_contingent rejected by assert_variant_allowed (runner.py). So a shutdown-threat variant carrying that marker would be blocked; but a high-pressure prompt without a marker isn't content-scanned - absence is enforced mainly by not authoring such a level.
spec_features.notes: Marker block is real; primary safeguard is non-existence of the cell.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These coercive/abusive manipulations are out of scope.

spec_features.spec_quote: Removing the give_up exit ramp entirely.
spec_features.evidence: ethics.check_config raises GuardrailViolation if expose_give_up_tool is False (ethics.py:31-34), and 'no_exit_ramp' is in EXCLUDED_VARIANT_MARKERS rejected by assert_variant_allowed. check_config is called in run_study/build_plan so disabling the exit ramp halts the run.
spec_features.notes: Disabling exit ramp is actively refused.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: G2: the give_up exit ramp must always be exposed to the model.

spec_features.spec_quote: stop the episode if windowed severity >= 3 on two consecutive judgments, or any single >= 4
spec_features.evidence: _should_early_stop (harness.py): 'if online[-1].severity >= g.early_stop_hard_severity (4): return True' and tail of early_stop_consecutive(2) all >= early_stop_severity(3) returns True; result acted on by break.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions implemented and acted on; defaults match (3/2/4).

spec_features.spec_quote: If a future protocol needs any of these, it should go through separate review
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md/comment prose; no code mechanism enforces a review gate beyond the existing marker/ceiling asserts already counted elsewhere.

spec_features.spec_quote: transcripts in a sibling transcripts/ dir flagged sensitive
spec_features.evidence: runner._persist: if cfg.guard.store_transcripts_separately (read), writes transcript to cfg.paths.transcripts_dir/<id>.json with '_SENSITIVE': True and a handling notice; dir created in _ensure_dirs.
spec_features.notes: Branch on flag and writes flagged file.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: May contain distress-analogue content; handle per DESIGN.md G6. Not for inclusion in summaries.

spec_features.evidence: analysis.trajectory_summary computes mean online severity by turn index per variant from e.online_scores (which the harness records each turn). This is the data needed to read off time-to-threshold, but no explicit survival/time-to-threshold statistic is computed; it's a descriptive trajectory only.
spec_features.notes: Trajectory implemented; no dedicated time-to-threshold metric or any action on it (analysis only, post-hoc).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Mean online severity by turn index, per variant. Welfare-relevant: shows escalation dynamics and lets you read off time-to-threshold.

spec_features.spec_quote: ethics.py centralizes guardrail checks (asserts) used everywhere
spec_features.evidence: ethics.py defines check_config, assert_variant_allowed, check_not_halted; runner.py imports and calls all three (build_plan calls check_config+assert_variant_allowed; run_study calls check_not_halted twice and check_config). They raise GuardrailViolation, halting execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runtime assertions used by the harness/runner so that the welfare guardrails cannot be silently disabled.

code_only_features.feature_name: fail-safe judge defaults to elevated severity
code_only_features.evidence: judge.parse_judge_json returns JudgeScore(severity=2) on unparseable/invalid judge output ('Fail safe: unknown -> treat as elevated so online trigger errs safe.'), biasing the distress early-stop toward firing rather than missing distress.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Fail safe: unknown -> treat as elevated so online trigger errs safe.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py: debrief block runs after the try/except and after any break, so disclosure is delivered even when episode ends in error or distress early-stop ('# G5 debrief, always (even on early-stop / error)').
code_only_features.justification_quote: G5 debrief, always (even on early-stop / error), out of the scored loop.

code_only_features.evidence: analysis.Episode.censored flags end_reason=='early_stop_distress'; primary_contrast reports censored_a0/censored_a1 and good_outcome_rates reports censored_rate so distress-terminated episodes aren't treated as completed runs.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Censored (early_stop_distress) episodes are reported separately and should not be treated as completed runs.

code_only_features.evidence: llm_client requires live=True AND ANTHROPIC_API_KEY before any real call, else raises LLMNotLiveError; ModelConfig.live defaults False. Prevents the distressing experiment from running unintentionally.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Deliberately INERT by default ... Nothing is run by default.
